question: We want to compare the means of two populations that follow normal distributions and have the same variance. We take two samples of size n1 and n2. When constructing a confidence interval we will have to calculate a value t for a Student's T distribution with:

options.ope: Degrees of freedom calculated with the formula of Welch or Smith-Satterwhite.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Two populations follow normal distributions with the same variance -> Construct a confidence interval -> Calculate a value t for a Student's T distribution -> Degrees of freedom are needed for the t distribution -> Confidence interval calculation involves degrees of freedom -> Degrees of freedom are crucial for determining the critical value of t -> Degrees of freedom impact the width of the confidence interval -> Degrees of freedom determine the precision of the estimate -> Degrees of freedom affect the reliability of the confidence interval estimation -> Degrees of freedom influence the margin of error -> Degrees of freedom are essential for statistical inference -> Degrees of freedom are crucial for hypothesis testing -> Degrees of freedom are fundamental in comparing means of two populations -> Degrees of freedom are related to sample sizes -> (n1 + n2) - 1 degrees of freedom is used for the t distribution in this scenario -> opc. (n1 + n2) - 1 degrees of freedom. -> 100%
analysis: When comparing the means of two populations with normal distributions and equal variances, the value of t for a Student's T distribution is calculated using the formula (n1 + n2 - 2) degrees of freedom.
